symptom: Vitest and Electron walkthrough runs leave nomi-* directories in the host temporary directory, growing local disks across repeated runs.
direct_cause: Temporary roots are created independently and cleanup is attached to individual happy-path scripts, so failed assertions, launch timeouts, and process exits bypass removal.
class_root: No shared lifecycle owner enforces creation and teardown for test-run and isolated Electron temporary roots.
affected_population: Vitest workers and every test using os.tmpdir()
Electron UX walks and E2E scripts using the shared launcher
Windows, Linux, and macOS repeated local or CI runs
entry_points: Vitest globalSetup creates one run root and redirects TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP
launchNomiApp registers isolated Electron profile roots
launcher close and process-exit teardown remove registered roots
internal_only_reason: The invariant is repository-owned test infrastructure lifecycle behavior; no vendor API decision controls it.
invariants: Every Vitest run has one owned root and restores the host temp environment after teardown.
Every isolated Electron launch registers its profile root before any child temp path is created.
Registered roots are removed on normal close, launch failure, and process exit, and cleanup is idempotent.

door_reduction.why_not: The Vitest constructor and its regression test are separate test-only doors; registerTempRoot and cleanupTempRoot are separate lifecycle operations in the shared Electron boundary. They cannot be merged without hiding either creation or teardown evidence.

generality_proof: Vitest workers inherit all three Node temp variables, so every existing and future os.tmpdir()/mkdtemp caller converges on the run root. Every isolated Electron caller converges on launchNomiApp, whose registry covers explicit and generated roots and has both close and process-exit teardown.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the Vitest run root, redirect inherited temp variables, and restore/remove them idempotently.
Own every isolated Electron profile root and remove it through the common cleanup boundary or process exit.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The config invokes tests/setup/tempWorkspace.ts before workers are created.
All shared Electron UX launches allocate or register their isolated profile root here.
startPlaybook delegates to launchCoreSmoke, which delegates to launchNomiApp; no second Electron launcher exists.

recurrence.reason: The same leak can be reintroduced by any new test or walk that creates a temp root, and existing failure paths already bypass per-script finally blocks.
same_class_scan: rg -n 'mkdtemp|mkdtempSync' tests scripts electron/testSupport found independent Vitest, UX, system, and walkthrough producers.
Checked tests/ux/_launchApp.mjs and tests/ux/full-walk/launch.mjs as the shared Electron launch chain.
Checked vitest.config.ts and tests/setup/* as the shared Vitest setup chain.

prevention.invariant: Each run owns its temp root and every owned root is removed on all lifecycle exits.
prevention.failure_mode: Cleanup is synchronous, idempotent, and fail-safe with force removal; no caller-specific exception path is required.
prevention.strategy: Move lifecycle ownership to global setup and the shared launcher registry, then keep individual tests focused on behavior rather than cleanup choreography.

legacy_paths.rationale: Existing callers remain compatible; the shared boundaries add lifecycle ownership without changing product or gate behavior.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls temporary-directory ownership.

migration: No persisted data or user files are migrated. Only roots created by the current test process are owned and removed.
residual_risks: Standalone scripts that never use the shared Electron launcher still require a later sweep; they are outside this shared-boundary change.
Existing historical nomi-* directories are intentionally untouched and require the coordinator's separate cleanup procedure.
